headline: On D1's actual output the refutation gate killed 4 of 17 TRUE positives and 0 of 3 FALSE positives, lowering precision from 0.850 to 0.813. It did the opposite of its purpose.
why_this_matters: Refutation is one of this pipeline's named anti-hallucination mechanisms, and the plan justifies it as 'the pattern that killed 3 of 4 false positives in the deterministic stages on 2026-08-15'. That number came from a DIFFERENT stage. Applied to D1, the check it was built to protect, it has no demonstrated false-positive benefit and a measurable true-positive cost. The `decided_by: "model+refutation"` label on D1 findings is accurate about the mechanism and, on this evidence, oversells what the mechanism buys.

caveats.sample_size: n=20 — every finding the 240-case run produced. A 4/17 kill rate has a wide interval; this is a direction, not a rate.
caveats.context_gap: The shipped gate is shown the FULL ABSTRACT. The checkpoint stored only the source_quote, so this replay showed the quote alone. The prompt's default is refuted=true, so LESS context makes refutation MORE likely: 4 killed true positives is an UPPER bound on the shipped gate. The zero killed false positives is NOT similarly bounded — with the full abstract the gate might catch some, and that is the open question.
caveats.prompt: REFUTE_SYSTEM is copied verbatim from claim-source.ts. An earlier paraphrase measured a different gate and killed 1 TP instead of 4, which is why the paraphrase was replaced.

what_to_do: Do NOT remove the gate on n=20. Re-run faithfully by re-resolving the 20 DOIs so the full abstracts are available, then decide. If the gate still buys nothing, D1's shipped precision equals its measured 0.944 and its recall is higher than the 0.215 upper bound currently recorded — both numbers move in our favour, which is exactly why this must not be left unmeasured.
